body:
Hey @DunklerPhoenix 
When we would implement this functionallity, how would you expect the hidden items to influence the board shown to you?
Would you like making some sort of disabled state for the app, to show the user that he is not able to use this app?

Heho
I would like to completly hide them like they don't exist. The other need to fill the space up i think

Filling up the space will not be possible, sorry. If you want to hide them in that way I only can suggest you to create seperate boards. Homarr will not be able to "fill up the space" as it does not know how you like the things placed in your board

But then we are at the other feature request with the mainboard per group. I really dont know hot to make this an elegant solution without showing all possible boards. Maybe i need to put an middleware in between which decides where to redirect based on group :/
I thought about it and I think graying them out would be enough

I would like if it they could just be hidden, I have many family members who will use this board and then come to me asking why they have a grey button or what "proxmox" and why it doesn't work when they press it.

> Filling up the space will not be possible, sorry. If you want to hide them in that way I only can suggest you to create seperate boards. Homarr will not be able to "fill up the space" as it does not know how you like the things placed in your board

How about, to start at least, if this option is only a thing for the category widgets. Since it takes up the entirety of the screen horizontally when one is hidden, it could just move everything up a row. It would work well enough for my use case at least.

It might be nice to at least have the option to hide applications from the applications section if the user doesn’t have access to them, because in most cases an application is just a link, and currently a user without permissions to create/edit applications can still see all applications created in the system, as well as the link leading to them. This is regardless of whether they are placed on boards the user has access to, or on boards they do not have access to.

Alternatively, it would be great to have an access control setting for the applications section itself, so that users without a specific group membership cannot see them.

On the boards themselves, if the user has access to the board, the application could either not be hidden at all, or its icon could be replaced with a generic lock icon, making it non-clickable and hiding its name as well.

It would be a fantastic feature to be able to completely hide apps based on user roles or groups, just as Dashy does.

This would make Homarr perfect for multi-user environments. Currently, all users can see all available apps. Ideally, a user should only see the apps they have permission to access.

This could be implemented using parameters similar to Dashy's:

hideForKeycloakUsers:
The item is visible to all Keycloak users, except for those in the specified groups or roles.
Ref: [Dashy Docs - hideForKeycloakUsers](https://dashy.to/docs/configuring/#sectiondisplaydatahideforkeycloakusers-sectiondisplaydatashowforkeycloakusers-itemdisplaydatahideforkeycloakusers-and-itemdisplaydatashowforkeycloakusers)

showForKeycloakUsers:
The item is hidden from all Keycloak users, and only shown to those in the specified groups or roles.
Ref: [Dashy Docs - showForKeycloakUsers](https://dashy.to/docs/configuring/#sectiondisplaydatahideforkeycloakusers-sectiondisplaydatashowforkeycloakusers-itemdisplaydatahideforkeycloakusers-and-itemdisplaydatashowforkeycloakusers)

This granular level of control would be a game-changer!

Apart from applications we want to share (e.g. jellyfin, jellyseerr, etc) there are administrative applications (e.g. adguard, portainer, etc.).  To prevent non admin users to see urls to the administrative apps which are available in the Apps List I finally ended up with two homarr instances, one instance for ordinary users and second instance for admins. I would like to have the possibility to hide availability of the App List and the Integrations List for non admin users.

> Apart from applications we want to share (e.g. jellyfin, jellyseerr, etc) there are administrative applications (e.g. adguard, portainer, etc.). To prevent non admin users to see urls to the administrative apps which are available in the Apps List I finally ended up with two homarr instances, one instance for ordinary users and second instance for admins. I would like to have the possibility to hide availability of the App List and the Integrations List for non admin users.

I am considering this at this time. I also don't believe anyone thinks that this is security, we more want this to help our less technically inclined users from complaining they clicked something and it denied them.
The simplest solution might be to add group permissions to have the  Apps and Integration Lists  available.

issue.title: feat: Apps and Integration lists are not visible by default to users in the everyone group.

repository.name: homarr
repository.description: A modern and easy to use dashboard. 40+ integrations. 20K+ icons built in. Authentication out of the box. No YAML, drag and drop configuration.

issue.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Apart from the applications we want to share (e.g., Jellyfin, Jellyseerr, etc.), there are also administrative applications (e.g., AdGuard, Portainer, etc.). Unfortunately, default users belonging to the everyone group can see the Apps and Integration lists, which include all URLs. To prevent non-admin users from seeing URLs to the administrative apps available in the Apps list, I ended up with two Homarr instances: one for regular users and another for admins. 

Instead of the  feature request #2078 Permission per App / App-Element / Dynamic Group I’d like a small improvement so that the Apps and Integration lists are not visible by default to users in the everyone group. The visibility of the Apps and Integration lists could be a group permission that’s granted optionally.
